structured_output.world_model:
W2 (empirical), after E052. Tip E049: 5.198 s, 0.7535 on seeds 0-2 (E036 + group-2 freeze over the last 10% + 0.25 epoch top-up). E050 reran the same code at 5.206 s and 0.7552. E036 reruns read 0.7532/0.7525/0.7497/0.7544. Rebuild noise is about 0.3 pp on a 3-seed mean and about ±0.03 s on time. Population mean is about 0.752, so headroom over the 0.75 bar is about 0.2 pp.

Mechanisms, with support:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch for 0.0-0.25 pp, roughly 1.5-2 s/pp (E020, E023, E027, E049).
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, confounded, E006) are already in the tip. More than 10 time-neutral boosters were flat or negative (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, wd, LS). Optimizer, averaging and regularization settings are flat within about 0.2 pp.
3. Time tracks pixels. Early 20 px is nearly free (E026, E033). Trimming steps or samples costs about as much as the dial (E031, E040, E041, E045, E048). E052 stacked selection with a top-up and read 4.987 s at 0.7555, so selection plus top-up looks slightly better than the dial, within noise.
4. Backward truncation is the best lever (E028, E034, E036, E046, E049). It is bandwidth-heavy. The group-2 freeze saves about 0.2-0.25 s at roughly neutral accuracy. Freezing group 1 at 60% is a cliff (E037, -0.38 pp). E039 and E042 saved only 0.03-0.05 s.
5. Architecture cuts cost accuracy at about the dial's rate or worse (E010, E021, E051). E051 saved 0.29 s but lost about 0.7 pp.
6. Non-step overhead is about 2.5% (E047). Systems work recovers at most about 1% (E035).
7. Noise: the 3-seed std is about 0.15-0.2 pp, and a rebuild alone moves the mean by 0.3 pp, so single-run differences under 0.3 pp are not resolvable. The kept tip is probably a lucky draw.

Misses: I under-predicted the savings of cuts and selection (E046, E048, E052 all came in faster than my range). I over-predicted time-neutral boosters. E052's time was 0.2 s below my range, so step-count cuts are cheaper than I model.

Unsure:
- Whether ReLU saves 3% or more. I expect 1-3%.
- Whether group 2 tolerates an 85% freeze. Each frozen step saves about 10 ms, so the extra 12 steps would save about 0.12 s. Accuracy cost is probably 0.05-0.15 pp.
- Whether the intermittent stem backward helps. It is plausible but untested.

forecasts.reason: About 12 more frozen steps save about 0.1 s. The accuracy change is under noise.
Same change as I082. The expected time saving is about 0.1 s and the accuracy effect is under the noise floor.
Half of about 71 steps skip stem backward at about 7 ms each, which saves about 0.25 s. The accuracy cost is uncertain, because the cliff in E037 suggests the stem needs gradients.
The freeze moves only 4% earlier, which saves about 0.07 s. The cliff probably sits between 60% and 71%, so the accuracy cost is modest.
The offline profile likely projects a 1-3% saving, below the 3% gate, so the step-2 run probably does not happen. If it does run, the numbers shown apply.
This stacks cuts with a top-up. It is conditional on earlier results, and it probably nets about 2-4% in time at flat accuracy.

cruxes: Is the build-to-build 3-seed accuracy spread (about 0.3 pp) removable by pinning kernel selection? If it is, margin decisions become resolvable.
Where is group 2's freeze cliff? A freeze at 85% or earlier that stays within 0.1 pp would unlock about 0.1-0.3 s.
Does ReLU, or any cheaper activation, save at least 3% of step time on this bandwidth-bound step?
